# BambooHR<>GrowthBook - Technical Discussion
Date: 2026-09-18 | Duration: 46m

## Summary
The team aligned on integrating Sanity CMS with GrowthBook to support granular content experimentation. Sanity schemas define editable components, while GrowthBook feature flags and experiments can swap component references or manage variant arrays through Sanity’s personalization plugin without coding changes. A proof of concept using self-hosted GrowthBook and a minimal Sanity build validated the core approach. One GrowthBook SDK instance can support both Sanity and Visual Editor experiments, with Next.js server-side rendering reducing flicker and client-side changes potentially causing brief flicker. Feature evaluation should occur near the point of use to avoid irrelevant bucketing. Consent-aware activation, session management, exposure callbacks, Adobe Analytics, Power BI, and SQL-compatible warehouses support privacy and reporting needs. GrowthBook and Sanity offered hands-on implementation support. The team reported strong confidence, no immediate blockers, and planned a Monday demo to confirm workflows and technical details.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, Sanity CMS, feature flags, personalization plugin, experimentation, Next.js

## Action Items

**Alan Lyes**
Continue preparing Sanity CMS setup with personalization plugin for integration with GrowthBook SDK, ensuring schema and experiment configurations are aligned (24:44)

**Jake Heier**
Share the recorded meeting and outline next steps to all participants to ensure alignment and preparation for upcoming demo (01:54)
Support BambooHR’s GrowthBook SDK integration and collaborate on preparations for the scheduled demo, providing technical guidance and troubleshooting as needed (35:27)

**Chris Sanders**
Provide technical support and collaborate on solutions around GrowthBook SDK integration with Sanity and visual editor experiments, including investigation of flicker minimization techniques (31:31)
Investigate and share options for minimizing flicker especially related to Next.js and SDK hydration strategies to improve user experience during experiments (17:06)

**James Collier**
Verify Adobe Analytics data flow and confirm backend data warehousing solutions for experiment reporting to ensure accurate and actionable insights (34:30)

**James Collier and Tom Scott**
Scope and finalize decision on usage of visual editor versus Sanity personalization plugin for different experimentation needs, balancing rapid testing and schema-driven experiments (10:58)

calls.title: BambooHR<>GrowthBook - Evaluation Discussion
calls.summary:
# MEDDICC Analysis: BambooHR & GrowthBook Evaluation Call

Call on [date not specified] with Lacee Jewkes (Marketing Operations, BambooHR), Jeff Smith (MOPS/Procurement, BambooHR), Tom Scott (BambooHR), James (BambooHR), Lauren (BambooHR), and Jake Heier (GrowthBook vendor).

## Attendees & Titles
Lacee Jewkes led the evaluation as the primary contact from BambooHR's marketing operations team, based remotely in Austin with occasional on-site presence in Salt Lake City. Jeff Smith joined from the MOPS team to handle procurement and vendor management processes. Tom Scott and additional team members (James, Lauren) participated in technical requirements discussions. Jake Heier represented GrowthBook as the account executive.

## Quantifiable Outcomes & Metrics
No specific ROI metrics or time savings were quantified during the discussion. However, pricing structures were discussed: Pro tier at approximately $40 per seat monthly, versus Enterprise with a $75,000 platform fee plus $1,000 per user annually. The transcript was incomplete regarding final pricing comparisons, though Jake noted that Enterprise pricing could potentially be more cost-effective than Pro depending on event volume factors in Pro's tiered pricing model.

## Budget Authority & Signals
Jeff Smith's presence indicated procurement authority and approval pathway involvement. Lacee Jewkes demonstrated budget consciousness by questioning service tier requirements and exploring creative workarounds (free accounts) to accelerate timelines while procurement processes completed. The discussion of platform fees and per-seat costs suggested budget constraints were a consideration.

## Technical Requirements
The primary technical requirement centered on Single Sign-On (SSO) capability, identified as a key differentiator between Pro and Enterprise tiers. BambooHR currently uses Okta for authentication, which Jake confirmed was compatible with GrowthBook's Enterprise SSO offering. The team also explored whether Google login could serve as an interim access method before full Okta implementation. Tom Scott indicated they needed account setup and access provisioning for the migration partner, Appnovation.

## Decision Process & Timeline
The decision timeline appeared compressed by an external migration initiative. Lacee articulated the urgency: BambooHR was mid-migration with Appnovation (the implementation vendor), and GrowthBook integration was blocking migration work. The team sought to separate the implementation timeline from procurement approval, requesting temporary free account access to proceed with migration work while formal procurement processes continued. Jake offered flexibility in account provisioning pending tier confirmation.

## Pain Points & Specific Needs
The primary pain point was procurement velocity conflicting with migration urgency. Lacee stated: "we're trying to figure out a way to start integrating growth book with our current migration and adding that work to existing sprints while we figure out the procurement, which takes time." The team needed to integrate GrowthBook into existing sprint workflows without delaying the broader BambooHR migration initiative.

## Champion Signals
Lacee Jewkes demonstrated strong champion behavior by proactively securing multiple stakeholder attendance, clearly articulating business drivers, and problem-solving creatively around constraints. She researched competitor precedents (mentioning Propound as an example of tools without SSO requirements) to determine if enterprise security mandates could be flexible.

## Competitors Mentioned
No direct competitors were mentioned during the call.

## Next Steps
The team agreed to research internal security and IT requirements regarding SSO mandates before final service tier selection. Lacee committed to consulting with colleagues about tier recommendations. Jake agreed to clarify pricing differentials
